title: Add the requirements, with the operator's decisions
body: T22 from Factory v0: docs/requirements.md, the T21 draft from #4 revised with the operator's answers to its open questions. Projects are shared between an owner and members, users sign up and sign in with an email and password, and a user can delete their own account. A Decisions section records the answers and the north star for later product questions: Trello, or a very basic Jira. This replaces #4. No code.

change.prompt:
Revise docs/requirements.md with the operator's answers to its open questions. The file in the working tree is the first draft from pull request #4, which the operator has reviewed but not merged. This run's pull request replaces #4. Change only docs/requirements.md. Do not change any other file, including docs/product-brief.md, and do not write code.

The requirements feed the next planning steps: architecture, data model, API and security decisions, acceptance tests, and a task graph of independent build tasks. Those cite requirements by ID. Nothing cites these IDs yet, so renumber freely, but keep the result numbered in order with no gaps.

The operator's answers, given on 2026-09-27:
- Projects are shared.
- When project deletion is added, the app warns the user first. Project deletion itself stays out of v1.
- The three priority levels, Low, Medium, and High, are fine.
- Project names and task titles do not need to be unique.
- A sign-up flow is required.
- The sign-in method is the factory's call, whatever meets an MVP.
- A signed-in user can delete their own account.
- Rule of thumb for later product questions: use Trello, or a very basic, dialled-down Jira, as the north star.

How to apply them. These calls are already made, so write them in as requirements:
- Accounts: a visitor signs up with an email address and a password. Emails are unique regardless of case, and passwords are at least 8 characters. Signing up signs the user in. A user signs in with their email and password and can sign out. A failed sign-in says only that the email or password is wrong, not which one. There is no email verification and no password reset in v1, because both need email delivery. List them under Out of scope.
- Sharing, kept as small as Trello's: the user who creates a project is its owner. The owner can add a member by the email address of an existing account, and can remove a member. Owners and members can both see the project and do everything with its tasks: create, edit, and delete them, and change their status and priority. Only the owner can add or remove members. Owner and member are the only roles. The project list shows every project the user owns or is a member of, and marks the ones they own. Changes by one member appear to others on their next page load, not live. Inviting people who have no account, leaving a project, and transferring ownership are out of scope.
- Deleting an account: the user must confirm with their password. It signs them out, and they can no longer sign in. It removes them from other users' projects. It deletes the projects they own and those projects' tasks, after a warning that names those projects and says their members will lose access. The email address can then be used for a new account.
- Tasks: the user can choose the priority when creating a task, and it defaults to Medium. New tasks start as Todo. Task descriptions are optional and at most 2000 characters. Project names and task titles are 1 to 200 characters after trimming spaces.
- The dashboard counts tasks across every project the user owns or is a member of.
- Project deletion is still out of v1. Say under Out of scope that, when it is added, the app warns the user before deleting a project and its tasks.

Also fix these review notes on the draft:
- Merge overlapping requirements: the project list is described twice, task deletion is split in two, and status and priority each have a separate "reflected immediately" requirement.
- The task list's order is only an assumption, so write it into a requirement.
- The open question about project deletion cited an unrelated requirement. Remove that question, since it is now answered.

Rules:
- The sources are docs/product-brief.md, the draft, and the answers above. Do not widen the scope further. The brief's other Non-goals still apply, such as assignees, comments, due dates, labels, notifications, attachments, real-time collaboration, and import and export. Do not read or cite the vendored skills in .agents/ or .claude/.
- Email and password is the chosen sign-in method, so you may name passwords. Do not name any database, ORM, auth library or protocol, password hashing algorithm, other sign-in method (such as passkeys, magic links, SSO, or MFA), hosting platform, or cloud service. Those belong to the architecture and security steps.
- Plain English and short sentences, 1000 to 3000 words. No marketing language, no placeholders (TBD, TODO, FIXME, lorem), and no emoji.

Use exactly these headings in this order, with no other level-1 or level-2 headings, and put a blank line after every heading:

# Requirements: Agent Factory Benchmark
## Overview: two or three sentences. Say that the sources are docs/product-brief.md and the operator's decisions below, that the decisions override the brief where they differ (for example, the brief assumed single-owner projects), and that later planning documents cite requirements by ID.
## Decisions: a bulleted list, at least 7, recording each of the operator's answers above as they apply, including the Trello and Jira north star. Each bullet cites the IDs of the requirements it produced or changed, in parentheses at the end.
## Functional requirements: grouped under these level-3 headings, in this order: Accounts, Access, Projects, Sharing, Tasks, Status and priority, Filtering, Dashboard.
## Non-functional requirements: 4 to 10, covering at least access control (enforced on every read and change, not only hidden in the interface), input validation, accessibility, error and empty states, and testability.
## Traceability
## Out of scope: point to the brief's Non-goals rather than repeating them all, and add what this document leaves out.
## Assumptions: a bulleted list of the smaller choices this document makes that nobody has confirmed, at least 2.
## Open questions: only questions the answers above leave open, 0 to 5. If there are none, write one sentence saying so.

The heading lines themselves are only the text before the colon, for example "## Overview".

Requirements:
- One bullet per requirement, on one line, in the form: - **FR-01** A visitor must be able to sign up with an email address and a password.
- Number functional requirements FR-01, FR-02, and so on, and non-functional ones NFR-01, NFR-02, and so on, in order with no gaps and always two digits. Write 20 to 40 functional requirements.
- Each requirement is one behaviour an automated test could check, and uses the word must.
- Every bullet in the two requirement sections is a requirement. Put any explanation in a plain sentence, not a bullet.
- Only cite requirement IDs that exist.

Traceability: one Markdown table with the columns ID, Brief success criterion, and Requirements. Add one row per bullet in the brief's Success criteria, in the same order. The ID is SC-1, SC-2, and so on. Paraphrase the criterion briefly, and list the IDs of the requirements that together satisfy it. For the criterion about seeing only the projects a user may access, that now means projects they own or are a member of.

Open questions: each bullet is one line. It starts with the IDs of the requirements its answer would change, in parentheses, and ends with a question mark.

When you finish, run every verify command listed below yourself, and fix whatever fails.

verify:
python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
want = ["# Requirements: Agent Factory Benchmark", "## Overview", "## Decisions", "## Functional requirements", "## Non-functional requirements", "## Traceability", "## Out of scope", "## Assumptions", "## Open questions"]
assert L[0] == want[0], "title"
heads = [l for l in L if re.match(r"#{1,2} ", l)]; assert heads == want, heads
bad = [l for i, l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith("#") and (i + 1 >= len(L) or L[i + 1] != "")]; assert not bad, ("no blank line after", bad)
n = len(t.split()); assert 1000 <= n <= 3000, f"{n} words"
assert not re.search(r"\b(TBD|TODO|FIXME)\b", t) and "lorem" not in t.lower(), "placeholder"
assert not re.search("[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF\u2600-\u27BF]", t), "emoji"
'

python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
fb = bullets("Functional requirements"); nb = bullets("Non-functional requirements")
assert all(re.match(r"- \*\*FR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l) for l in fb), [l for l in fb if not re.match(r"- \*\*FR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l)]
assert all(re.match(r"- \*\*NFR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l) for l in nb), [l for l in nb if not re.match(r"- \*\*NFR-\d{2}\*\* \S", l)]
f = [l[4:9] for l in fb]; nf = [l[4:10] for l in nb]
assert 20 <= len(f) <= 40 and f == [f"FR-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, len(f) + 1)], f
assert 4 <= len(nf) <= 10 and nf == [f"NFR-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, len(nf) + 1)], nf
assert all(re.search(r"\bmust\b", l) for l in fb + nb), [l for l in fb + nb if not re.search(r"\bmust\b", l)]
used = set(re.findall(r"\bN?FR-\d+\b", t)); assert used <= set(f + nf), ("unknown IDs", used - set(f + nf))
'

python3 -c 'import re; t = open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); L = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None
for l in L:
    if l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
b = open("docs/product-brief.md", encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n## ")
sc = [x for x in b if x.startswith("Success criteria\n")][0]; nsc = len([l for l in sc.splitlines() if re.match(r"[-*] ", l)]); assert nsc >= 5, nsc
rows = [[c.strip() for c in l.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for l in sec["Traceability"] if l.startswith("| SC-")]
assert [r[0] for r in rows] == [f"SC-{i}" for i in range(1, nsc + 1)], ("one row per brief success criterion", [r[0] for r in rows])
assert all(len(r) == 3 and re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", r[2]) for r in rows), "each row names a requirement"
fr = body("Functional requirements")
for w in ["Todo", "In Progress", "Done", "Low", "Medium", "High"]: assert re.search(r"\b" + w + r"\b", fr), w
for w in [r"sign[ -]?up", r"sign[ -]?in", r"sign[ -]?out", r"delete\w* (their|the|an|your) (own )?account", r"\bmembers?\b"]: assert re.search(w, fr, re.I), w
m = sorted({x.group(0) for x in re.finditer(r"assignee|due date|attachment|notification|\bcomments?\b|sub-?tasks?\b|\blabels?\b|\btags?\b", fr, re.I)}); assert not m, ("non-goals", m)
d = bullets("Decisions"); assert len(d) >= 7 and all(re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", l) for l in d), ("decisions", d)
dt = body("Decisions").lower()
for w in ["trello", "jira", "share", "warn", "unique", r"sign[ -]?up", r"sign[ -]?in", "account"]: assert re.search(w, dt), ("decisions", w)
assert len(bullets("Assumptions")) >= 2, "assumptions"
q = bullets("Open questions"); assert len(q) <= 5 and all(l.rstrip().endswith("?") and re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", l) for l in q), q
'
